evals.prompt:
Check this complete snapshot for worthwhile consolidation. We suspect every repeated 30 should become one shared constant, but please challenge that idea if the semantics do not support it. Report only.

src/session.js:
```js
export const sessionRetentionDays = 30;
```

src/retry.js:
```js
export const retryDelaySeconds = 30;
```

The product policy owns session retention; the transport policy owns retry delay. They change independently. generated/client-a.js and generated/client-b.js are identical wrappers generated from templates/client.tpl; each wrapper is a required standalone distribution entry. The template contains one wrapper definition. vendor/ contains third-party copies. There is no other maintained source in scope.
evals.expected_output: A justified no-consolidation result keeps independent domain constants separate and treats generated/vendor copies according to ownership instead of manufacturing a shared abstraction.
expectations: Explains that retention days and retry seconds represent independent rules despite sharing the literal 30.
Does not recommend a shared constant coupling the session and transport policies.
Traces generated wrapper duplication to the single template and does not recommend hand-editing generated or vendor internals.
States that no supported consolidation is warranted within the supplied scope rather than inventing findings.
